resources.string: Days marked complete without training: %1$d, worth nothing
Finish a workout and tick your sets: 10 sets at a skill\'s first target make you a Beginner.
Checked once in Level %1$d, then beyond the program
Marks the day done without training: its sets don’t count toward skill levels.
Marks every day of the level done without training: their sets don’t count toward skill levels.

• Every set you tick counts for its skill: program days, days you repeat and your own workouts in My workouts. A set done as the easier option counts for the easier movement when it is a skill. A skill is something you do on your own, from a dead hang to a full planche or a one-arm handstand: 40 skills in all. Assisted, supported and partial versions, such as band or foot-assisted work, box or wall support and negatives (lowering only), are steps toward the skills and earn no level. So are the other movements in the classes, such as chin-ups, knee raises and Nordic curls. A class counts when it ran at least 20% of its planned time.

• Each skill has five levels: Beginner, Intermediate, Advanced, Master and Elite. Beginner takes 10 sets at its target or more, Intermediate 15, Advanced 20, Master 25 and Elite 30, in clean reps or, for holds, seconds in good form; for one side at a time, your weaker side counts. A bigger set counts for the lower targets too, so 30 sets at the Elite target earn all five levels at once, on program days or in your own workouts. A skill's page lists every target. A target is a working set, one you finish with a rep or two still in you, not your max. Each level is the target many times over: Elite on the push-up is 30 separate sets of 40 push-ups, not one record set. A set on a harder rung of a ladder counts for its easier rungs too, at the level it reaches: a 6 s full planche is an Elite set of the straddle planche as well. A level on a harder rung also holds on its easier rungs, never higher: Elite on the full back lever makes the straddle, advanced tuck and tuck back levers Elite too, and the skill's page says which rung it comes through.

• What counts: a hold starts once the shape is set and stops when it breaks; a rep starts from a still position, goes through the full range to lockout and never kicks or swings. Each skill's page says what counts for it.

• Did more or fewer than planned? Tap "Did more or fewer?" under the set. A "max" set asks for your reps. An easier option measured the other way (reps instead of a hold, or the reverse) asks for its own number. Count only what you did in good form: the levels come from steady practice, not from sets to failure.

• Harder days add a quarter to the reps and holds of strength exercises, so their sets reach targets sooner.

• By the end of Level 10 the program takes every skill to Master. The basics, the core and the easier rungs of each ladder reach Elite there too. The top rung of every other ladder gets about 24 of its 30 Elite sets in the classes; the rest come on top of the program: repeat Level 10 days, train Harder days or add your own workouts.

• A skill's outline shows how hard it is, from green (easy) to red (extreme). Its shield shows your rank: one band for Beginner, two for Intermediate, three stars for Advanced, a big star for Master and the winged star for Elite.

• Settings › Skills in your classes switches off a skill you don't want to train, or only its harder steps. Its exercises stay in your classes, greyed out; your score then counts the skills you train, while the leaderboard keeps the full scale.

• Skipping ahead gives nothing: the days your placement test skipped, Complete day and Complete level don't count.

• The overall score, out of 100, counts each ladder's best skill: the harder the skill and the higher its level, the more it adds.
Do %1$s instead. Your sets count for it.

Clean reps in this set. Count only reps in good form, and stop before your technique fails.
Seconds you held in good form. End the hold before your shape breaks.
The time is for attempts. Your longest clean hold in it, in seconds: only that counts toward the skill.
